findings.text: s13's done-when pins the nine-implementations, three-reviews case to "the same seats in the same order", but with the deliverable applied the order changes at seat 8 while both roles still wait: `_seat_share_turns` gives `I R I I R I I R I I I I` and `weighted_project_order` keyed on the role gives `I R I I R I I I R I I I I` for that exact slice (measured at revision 68a11d72 against `reckon/crew/admission/ordering.py` with the module's own `_role_seat_weights`, weights 0.692/0.308). The current test asserts no order at all — `test_a_pass_gives_both_roles_a_seat_with_three_waiting` only checks membership in the first three seats — so this arm is a demand no existing assertion carries, and it contradicts the deliverable two lines above it

findings.reason: the section's stated root cause is "a duplicate that agrees seat for seat", and the change it asks for is a behaviour change to the seat cadence, which the plan must state as such or the reuse is argued on a premise the code does not support.
findings.text: the `Why.` justifies the reuse on "From a zero start the two accrual keys agree seat for seat", which the cited module falsifies: with three implementations and nine reviews the quota key seats an implementation first (`I R R R I R R I R R R`) while `weighted_project_order` seats a review first (`R I R R I R R R I R R R`), because it accrues a role's weight before choosing and the quota key compares after, so the two differ at the first seat whenever the shares are unequal and at seat 8 of the plan's own nine/three case

findings.reason: a worker following the text either widens an interface the plan says to reuse or silently rewrites the field the surrounding pass groups on, and no done-when arm checks the project field afterwards.
findings.text: `weighted_project_order(ordered, weights)` takes no key argument and groups rows by `pointer["project"]` (`reckon/crew/admission/ordering.py:70-105`), returning the same mapping objects it was given; "computed through `weighted_project_order` with the role as its key" therefore describes a call the module does not offer, and the obvious way to supply a role key — passing copies whose `project` field carries the role — puts those copies back into the pass's order with `project` rewritten, a field `role_share_order`'s callers and the project slice keep reading

findings.reason: the reuse half's premise is itself disputed (the two findings above), so one close verdict would either carry a rename through a reverted reuse or leave the rename unreviewed, and each half is closable on its own gate.
